scenes.visual: carbon and electrons through three boxes
scenes.narration: Converting pyruvate to acetyl-CoA is not one reaction but three, carried out in sequence by a single complex. First comes decarboxylation, where pyruvate loses carbon dioxide, and the remaining two-carbon fragment is captured on thiamine pyrophosphate. Second is oxidation, where two electrons leave and the fragment is handed to the lipoamide arm. Third is transfer to coenzyme A, producing acetyl-CoA. Follow the carbon across the three boxes and follow the electrons separately, because those electrons end up reducing NAD⁺ to NADH. Notice that each step uses its own coenzyme, and several of those coenzymes trace back to B vitamins.

scenes.visual: lipoamide arm swings between E1, E2, E3
scenes.narration: Watch the lipoamide arm make its rounds. Tethered to the E2 core, it first swings to E1 and picks up the acetyl group, becoming acetyl-lipoamide. Next, it pivots back to E2 and delivers that acetyl unit to coenzyme A, releasing acetyl-CoA and leaving the arm reduced as dihydrolipoamide. Finally, it reaches E3 to be reoxidized, regenerating the disulfide so the cycle can repeat. Because the arm rides on a mobile lipoyl domain and the E2 core has many copies, 24 or 60 depending on the organism, all three active sites stay within reach. The intermediates never escape. They ride the tethered arm from station to station.

scenes.visual: timeline of four steps, NADH only at the last
scenes.narration: Let me put the whole mechanism on one timeline so you know exactly where NADH is born. Step one, decarboxylation on E1, releases carbon dioxide and makes no NADH. Step two, oxidative transfer, hands the hydroxyethyl group to lipoamide as it is oxidized to an acetyl group, still no NADH. Step three, acetyl transfer on E2, produces acetyl-CoA and leaves dihydrolipoamide, again, no NADH. Only in step four, regeneration on E3, is the reduced lipoamide reoxidized by FAD and the electrons flow onward to make NADH. So three steps build the product and exactly one step, the last, generates the reducing power.

scenes.narration: Enzyme E1 is the key regulatory site of the entire complex, and it is controlled by a simple on-off switch built from a kinase and a phosphatase that travel with the complex. A kinase phosphorylates E1 and inactivates it. A phosphatase removes that phosphate and reactivates it. The switch reads the cell's energy state. When ATP, acetyl-CoA and NADH are abundant, signaling plenty of fuel and product, the complex is inhibited. When ADP and pyruvate accumulate, signaling demand and available substrate, the complex is stimulated. So the gateway from glycolysis to the citric acid cycle opens only when the cell actually needs to burn pyruvate.
